Proposed scope

1.1 Platform

Migrate the storefront to Shopify. Ramatuelle already has a proven Shopify migration with LitOS on their first site, tuintrend.nl.

1.2 Theme — Ella (HaloThemes)

Recommend Ella (HaloThemes) as the base theme. Ella is a paid theme (ThemeForest, $79 regular price), but LitOS has a direct partnership with HaloThemes, so the license comes at no cost to the client — a meaningful saving given the client's budget sensitivity.

Why Ella specifically: it's a fashion/apparel-oriented theme, so it needs less customization than a generic theme to match Ramatuelle's category. It also ships with native Wishlist (dedicated wishlist page, header icon+counter) and native Product Compare as built-in theme features — not third-party apps. This gives full feature parity with the current site's wishlist/compare out of the box, no custom code required (see cost impact in Section 2).

1.3 Languages & currencies

Current site runs NL / EN / DE / ES and EUR / GBP / USD. Recommend Shopify Markets for currency conversion — native to Shopify, no extra app cost.

For languages, recommend T Lab ‑ AI Language Translate (Sherpas Design) — its free plan AI-translates up to 500 products and covers all three languages Ramatuelle needs (DE, NL, ES), which comfortably fits the store's likely catalog size at no extra cost. It also handles image and third-party-app text, glossary management for consistent terminology, and SEO/URL translation.

Alternative worth flagging: Langwill: AI Language Translate (Channelwill) — broader language coverage (138 languages) and its own geolocation-based currency switching, but its free tier is much tighter (5,000 words, 1 language only); would need the Starter plan ($9.99/mo, 5 languages / 30,000 words) to cover all three languages here. T Lab's free tier is the better fit for this store's budget unless the client specifically wants Langwill's feature set.

1.4 Homepage, category & page structure

Rebuild the current site structure on Ella: Home, product category/collection pages, product page, Lookbook, About/Our Story, Shipping & Returns, Size chart, and other standard pages — mirroring the current information architecture rather than introducing a new one.

1.5 Existing features to replicate

  • Wishlist & Compare — native in Ella, no app or custom build needed (Section 1.2)
  • Newsletter signup — native Ella Newsletter section (theme customizer block), no app needed
  • Homepage video banner — native Ella section, supports video backgrounds out of the box, no app needed
  • Instagram feed — native Ella Instagram section (theme customizer block), no app needed
  • Size chart — not a native Ella feature; recommend Kiwi Sizing (free to install; paid plans from $6.95–$24.95/mo depending on tier, with a small extra fee at higher monthly order volumes — unlikely to matter at Ramatuelle's current scale)
  • Trustpilot badge — official Trustpilot Shopify app, free tier available (50 review invites/mo, 1 widget), which is enough to keep the badge live; existing Trustpilot review history carries over as-is since it's platform-independent

1.6 Data migration — out of scope

Not included in this quote. Migrating products, product images, customers, order history and blog content is handled separately by LitExtension (LitE), who will quote the client directly for that piece. This proposal covers only the LitOS storefront/theme rebuild described above.

Improvement Ideas

Suggested improvements and follow-up ideas from the current Ramatuelle site walkthrough. These are not costed in the base quote unless explicitly scoped as part of a later phase.

1. Header

Move login/wishlist into icons next to the cart icon; move the language/currency switcher next to search.

2. Hero

Remove the dark overlay behind the hero text — reads cleaner without it.

3. Homepage category section

Current layout:

4. Homepage product section

Add a featured-products section to the homepage — not present on the current site.

5. Homepage banner

Current banner is small. For a fashion storefront, a larger banner better showcases product imagery, helps shoppers absorb the brand's style, and encourages further browsing.

6. Collection sidebar info → footer services section

This information currently sits in the collection-page sidebar — better suited as a global "services" section in the footer, visible site-wide instead of only on collection pages.

7. Collection page filters

Move all filters into a sidebar layout.

8. Product page

Show size/colour variant availability directly on the page, so shoppers immediately see what's in or out of stock — one less click than the current site.
